blurb: Largest of the bearded Schnauzers, a Bavarian farm guard turned police dog
description: The Giant Schnauzer is a large German working dog with a dense, wiry, weatherproof coat and a distinct beard, bred to drive livestock and guard property.
answer: The Giant Schnauzer, or Riesenschnauzer, is a German breed and the largest of the three Schnauzer breeds. It typically stands about 60 to 70 cm tall and weighs around 35 to 47 kg. Bred as a farm and guard dog, it is now widely used for police work and dog sports.

body: Schnauzers originated in southern Germany and share their history with the German Pinscher; the rough-haired type was renamed from Rauhaarige Pinscher to Schnauzer in 1917. The Giant Schnauzer was bred as a multipurpose farm dog to guard property and drive animals to market, and by around 1900 it guarded factories, breweries, butcheries and stockyards in Bavaria. It was unknown outside Bavaria until it served as a military dog in both World Wars. The first dogs reached America in the 1930s, and the breed became popular there in the 1960s.

Large, stocky and square in shape, the Giant Schnauzer should resemble a bigger Standard Schnauzer. Its name is giant only in comparison with the Standard and Miniature Schnauzers. The coat is dense, wiry and weather resistant, with a distinct beard and eyebrows, in pepper and salt, pure black, or black and silver. Ears are small and high-set; where legal, ears may be cropped and tails docked.

The breed is commonly described as alert, which is one reason it is used in police work. In Europe it is regarded more as a working dog than a show dog, and in several countries, including Germany, dogs must earn a Schutzhund title before becoming conformation champions.

Giant Schnauzers take part in obedience, agility, herding, search and rescue, nosework, carting and Schutzhund. As a large working breed it is generally expected to need regular exercise and training, and the wiry coat and beard benefit from regular grooming.

Conditions reported in the breed include hip and elbow dysplasia, eye problems such as glaucoma, cataracts and progressive retinal atrophy, skin conditions, and skin cancers in dark-colored dogs, as well as hypothyroidism and seizure disorders. In a Kennel Club survey the most common causes of death were lymphoma and liver cancer. A 2024 UK study found a life expectancy of 12.1 years.

faq.q: How big does a Giant Schnauzer get?
faq.a: Giant Schnauzers typically stand about 60 to 70 cm at the withers and weigh roughly 35 to 47 kg, with males larger than females.

faq.q: How long do Giant Schnauzers live?
faq.a: A 2024 UK study found a life expectancy of 12.1 years for the breed.

faq.q: What colors do Giant Schnauzers come in?
faq.a: There are three color varieties: pepper and salt, pure black, and black and silver.

faq.q: Is the Giant Schnauzer recognized by the FCI?
faq.a: Yes. The FCI lists it as breed number 181 in Group 2.
